sla_onsite.text: onID="2.0.2">CRITERION.EXCLUSION.CONVICTIONS.PARTICIPATION_IN_CRIMINAL_ORGANISATION</cbc:CriterionTypeCode> <cbc:Name>Osalemine kuritegelikus organisatsioonis</cbc:Name> <cbc:Description languageID="ET">Kas ettevõtja ise või tema haldus-, juht- või järelevalveorgani liige või isik, kellel on volitused seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on lõpliku süüdimõistva kohtuotsusega süüdi mõistetud kuritegelikus organisatsioonis osalemise eest kõige rohkem viimase viie aasta jooksul või kehtib süüdimõistvas kohtuotsuses sätestatud kõrvalejäämise kohustus endiselt?</cbc:Description> <cac:Legislation> <cbc:ID schemeID="CriteriaTaxonomy" schemeAgencyID="EU-COM-GROW" schemeVersionID="2.0.2">c753a2c5-59e6-4970-b6eb-27224e96bf76</cbc:ID> <cbc:Title languageID="ET">RHS § 95 lg 1 p 1 "keda või kelle haldus-, juhtimis- või järelevalveorgani liiget, prokuristi või muud isikut, kellel on volitus seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on karistatud kuritegelikus ühenduses osalemise eest". Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. ion. 1.6.3 Delivered product shall integrate A-GRA autonomy interface into the existing MTS Service Set creation tool. Upon selection of A-GRA, the Mission Planner Autonomy UI must dynamically reconfigure connection parameter fields (e.g., IPs, Ports, Serial) to match the A- GRA interface format and auto -populate with appropriate default values. The delivered product shall include unique A-GRA–based service sets that preserve all existing autopilot and MTS configuration properties and differ only by using the A-GRA Autonomy Interface in place of legacy autonomy interfaces. 1.6.4 Delivered product shall maintain existing MTS Run Time Assurance (RTA) safety behaviors (e.g., geofencing, vehicle constraints, remediation) when A-GRA is the active autonomy provider and shall handle malformed or missing A-GRA/UCI messages without crashing or degrading RTA enforcement. 1.6.5 Product documentation (e.g., user guidance, configuration instructions, and build/install procedures) shall be delivered as part of this contract to describe how to enable, configure, and operate the A-GRA Autonomy Interface, A- GRA Message Processor, A-GRA service sets, and any other changes to MTS implemented under this effort, and shall clearly specify how the delivered product operates on existing MTS TA

SCOPE OF SERVICE The Contractor shall provide enterprise -grade mobile and data services to the U.S. Embassy Panama. The prices listed below shall include all labor, service, equipment, technical support, materials, insurance (see FAR 52.228 -4 and 52.228- 5), overhead, and profit. The Government will pay the Contractor on a monthly basis for routine services that have been satisfactorily performed. The Contractor shall ensure that all services are delivered with high availability, reliability, and performance consistent with commercial best practices for enterprise telecommunications services. The Contractor shall offer two different plans to fulfill the Government needs: Basic Plan. Pay per use for actual calls (local, local long distance, international long distance), incoming and outgoing roaming calls, incoming and outgoing local SMS, incoming and outgoing international SMS, incoming and outgoing roaming SMS. Unlimited Smart Phones & Tablets Plan. A flat monthly rate per cellphone line that includes unlimited: local data, local minutes on-net, local minutes off-net, national long-distance minutes,

International calling services shall support clear and reliable voice communications consistent with the best commercial practices for enterprise telecommunications services. INTERNATIONAL ROAMING The Contractor shall provide broad international roaming coverage for voice, SMS, and data services through commercially established roaming agreements with foreign mobile network operators. Emphasis shall be placed on roaming availability and service reliability throughout the Western Hemisphere. The Contractor shall support international roaming services compatible with 4G/LTE services, and/or 5G services (5G services where commercially available). The Contractor shall provide the COR with an updated list of current international roaming partners and supported roaming countries at least every six (6) months. The Contractor shall disclose any significant roaming restrictions, unsupported regions, or service limitations in its proposal. SMS MESSAGING The Contractor shall provide reliable SMS messaging services on a 24- hour basis, including domestic, inter

ns and changes, lost or stolen device r eporting, billing inquiries, and service troubleshooting. The Contractor shall provide dedicated account management and support personnel who are fluent in both English and Spanish. The Contractor shall provide a dedicated customer support email address for the U.S. Embassy Panama. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. public health through development of data and knowledge that are translatable, predictive, and timely. The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based m

The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based microphysiological systems and test methods that better model human health (in this case, the initial work will focus on liver). 3) Scope: The Contractor shall provide a Fluigent Microencapsulation Platform, in accordance with the obtained vendor quotation. The system shall include the require

formation of three-dimensional (3D) microtissues and organoids. The Contractor shall also provide installation and training for the Fluigent system at the NIEHS facility. Vendor representatives shall perform system setup and provide training to facilitate rapid onboarding and use of the technology. The system will operate independently of NIEHS information technology (IT) systems and will not require NIEHS IT support. The computer and software components are expected to be delivered by the end of September 2026. Full system installation and training are expected to be completed in Fall 2026, subject to vendor engineer scheduling availability. The Government will make the determination of relevance (based on size, scope, and complexity of requirement). Contracts/orders listed may include those entered into with the Federal Government, agencies of state and local governments and commercial concerns. Offerors may also submit past performance information regarding predecessor companies, key personnel who have relevant experience or subcontractors that will perform major or critical aspects of the requirement when such information is relevant to the acquisition. For the purposes of this solicitation, a major subcontract is defined as 20% of the total contract effort. Data concerning the prime contractor shall be provided first, followed by each proposed major subcontractor, in alphabetical order. Offerors shall indicate on Attachment F if there are Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) / Past Performance Information Retrieval System (PPIRS) report(s) available for each reference.
